Project Confluence — Assembling a Four-Sided Building Shell

Extending a two-facade corner into a four-sided building shell, testing how different facade layouts affect its footprint, and moving the placement logic into a reusable Blueprint function.

ContentsCheck how the corner responds to a layout changePlace all four facadesExtract the placement logic into a function

Check how the corner responds to a layout change

The previous building prototype used two modular facades to test how a corner responds to changes in module spacing. This time, I changed the column count of the first facade. When the building’s Construction Script ran again, the second facade moved to the expected position. This confirmed that a change to the facade layout could drive the placement of an adjoining wall.

Place all four facades

I extended BP_ModularBuilding to place four facade actors around a rectangular footprint. Facade A provides the reference, and the Blueprint uses the spans of the adjoining walls to position the other sides. At the corners, B and D are offset to leave the thickness of the A and C walls visible. I adjusted the rotations of C and D to 180° and 90°, respectively, so that their module layouts extended in the intended directions.

One editor comparison shows Facade B in two configurations, with two columns and three columns. Both use a module width of 200 cm and two floors. The opening arrangement also differs between the two views, which show how the four walls meet around footprints of different depths.

Extract the placement logic into a function

Once the four walls were positioning as expected, I moved the placement logic into PositionFacades. The function calculates Facade A’s span from its column count and module width, then uses half the wall thickness when setting Facade B’s relative position. BuildFacade handles the arrangement of modules on each wall, and PositionFacades determines how the walls meet. The next step is to fit a roof to the assembled footprint before developing balcony, railing, and shading components for the residential prototype.
